newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends unchanged despite U.S. long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends unchanged despite U.S. long bond.

text.p: Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts ended flat for the second session in a row on Friday after what traders said was a quiet day in the runup to the May 20 Federal Open market Committee meeting.
"U.S. long bond yields climbed and the Dow Jones fell, but the peso came under no pressure as dealers have mostly squared positions," a trader said.
The 48-hour peso ended unchanged at 7.8930/7.8960 while its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.8 of a centavo weaker at 7.8900/7.8930 per dollar.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were dowmn 16/32 to yield 6.91 percent in late trade, while the Dow Jones had fallen 121.57 points to 7,211.98.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 0.4 of a centavo firmer at 7.8810/7.8840 per dollar.
Dealers forecast a trading range of 7.8850/7.9250 per dollar for the 48-hour peso on Monday.
"Next week will much depend how U.S. (financial) markets react to the FOMC meeting," a trader said.
